our_title: amk_grf hands un-based label matches to the library; no list range check anywhere
ran: See /tmp/claude-1000/-home-dev-workspace-pyscotch/087f3d41-a5d8-4b0a-9260-769d70cf8179/scratchpad/work/G27-seq-tools/repro/CLI-11/README. Pristine ($INFRA/asan): `amk_grf -llab.lst lab_b1.grf` -> `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ ... #0 graphInduceList graph_induce.c:138 #1 archDecoArchBuild arch_deco_build.c:196 #2 SCOTCH_archBuild0`; `amk_grf -lm4x4_vertlist.txt m4x4_b1_elv.grf` (labelled base-1 check data) -> no sanitizer report but a garbage deco file (rows `-1 0 0`, zero distances) where the base-0 twin gives a valid one; `amk_grf unl_b1.grf -lbad.lst` (values 3 90) -> heap-buffer-overflow WRITE graph_induce.c:137; api_list b/i (SCOTCH_archBuild0 / SCOTCH_graphInduceList with list {0,99}) -> same overflow. Patched (32 and 64-bit): base-0 and base-1 outputs differ only in the terminal label column (+1); bad list -> `main: list vertex number out of range` rc=1; API -> `graphInduceList: invalid vertex list`, return 1.
severity_note: Higher than the review's medium: not only the tool, the public SCOTCH_archBuild0() and SCOTCH_graphInduceList() write out of bounds on any out-of-range list entry (heap WRITE in graph_induce.c:137); for labelled base-1 graphs the tool silently writes a wrong architecture even when ASan is quiet.
evidence: amk_grf.c:205 `sorttab[vertnum].vertnum = vertnum;` (0-based), :218 `listtab[listnum] = sorttab[vertnum ++].vertnum; /* Replace label by number */`; arch_deco_build.c:196 `graphInduceList (tgtgrafptr, tgtlistnbr, tgtlisttab, &jobtab[0].grafdat);` (status ignored), :301 `tgtvertnum = (tgtlisttab != NULL) ? tgtlisttab[termdomnum] : (termdomnum + tgtgrafptr->baseval);`; graph_induce.c:137 `orgindxtax[orgvertnum] = indvertnum;` with no check; doc s_l.tex:1990 `These indices should have the same base value as the one of the graph`.
review_accuracy: Accurate on both sub-claims and on the location. Its Fix line (store vertnum + baseval, reject out-of-range values) is correct for the tool but leaves the public API SCOTCH_archBuild0()/SCOTCH_graphInduceList() unprotected and does not mention that archDecoArchBuild() ignores graphInduceList()'s status.
first_pass_critique: Status/method/evidence correct. Its preferred option (tool only) is incomplete: the same overflow is reachable through two public API routines, and archDecoArchBuild() also ignores the status of graphInduceList() and of archDecoArchBuild2() (PS2-G27-1), so even a library check would have been ineffective without the caller fix. Its range check is fine but was put in a restructured if/else; ours keeps the sorted-list bound test. It did not notice that archDeco2ArchBuild() already does the unconditional check (precedent) nor that the type-2 path rejects base 1 anyway.

severity_note: Agrees with the review: silent wrong output files for any base-1 graph (check_prog_gout itself feeds base-100000 graphs to both writers and only looks at the return code).

evidence: gout_o.c:405 `fprintf (fileptr, "\t" SCOTCH_NUMSTRING ",", indxtab[indxnum] - baseval); /* Un-base vertex indices in paths */` (applied to -1 terminators too); :1121 `indxtab[indxnbr ++] = verttmp;` :1142 `indxtab[indxnbr ++] = verttmp;` :1175 `fprintf (fileptr, SCOTCH_NUMSTRING "\t", indxtab[indxnum ++]);` while :1160 writes POINTS for vertnum = baseval..vertnnd-1 in order.

our_title: atst seeds its minimum distance with -1 on 32-bit SCOTCH_Num, NUMMAX leaks for one terminal
ran: repro/CLI-13: pristine 32-bit `atst c8.tgt` (cmplt 8) -> `min=-1 max=1`; cmplt 1 -> `min=-1`; `amk_m2 4 4 | atst` -> `min=-1 max=6`. Pristine 64-bit: cmplt 8 -> min=1, cmplt 1 -> `min=9223372036854775807`. Patched 32 and 64: min=1 / min=0 / min=1. check_prog_atst, check_prog_amk, check_prog_amk_grf pass on both.
severity_note: Agrees (wrong statistic in a diagnostic tool).
evidence: atst.c:161 `distmin = (SCOTCH_Num) (((unsigned long) ((SCOTCH_Num) -1)) >> 1); /* Set to maximum number in Anum */`; scotch.h:78 `#define SCOTCH_NUMMAX ((int) (((unsigned int) 1 << ((sizeof (int) << 3) - 1)) - 1))` (64-bit: int64_t/uint64_t variants); library uses GNUMMAX = INTVALMAX (graph.h:104, common.h:277) which is not in the public header.
review_accuracy: Mechanism accurate. Its first suggested expression `(unsigned SCOTCH_Num) ~0` is not valid C (SCOTCH_Num is a typedef); its second (SCOTCH_NUMMAX) is the public, size-correct macro, already used by gotst.c:235.
first_pass_critique: Correct, and it noticed the single-terminal case prints the sentinel; it still preferred the plain SCOTCH_NUMMAX. We take its remark into the fix: `(termnbr > 1) ? SCOTCH_NUMMAX : 0`, consistent with how distavg already treats termnbr <= 1 three lines below.

extra_instances.quote: no other sentinel computed this way; gmk_ub2.c:176 `(vertnum >> 1)` is a genuine halving

our_title: gmk_m2 -e -t header subtracts overlapping removed arcs twice when both dimensions < 3
ran: repro/CLI-18: pristine sweep d0,d1 in 1..4 with -e -t: 1x1 header=-4 written=0, 1x2 -2/2, 2x1 -2/2, 2x2 8/12, all `gtst: ERROR: graphLoad: invalid number of edges|arc count`; other 12 sizes header==written. Patched 32/64: all 16 load. Byte comparison with pristine 7.0.17 gmk_m2 over 150 (dims 1..5 x 6 flag sets): 142 identical, the 8 differing files are exactly the -e -t ones with d0,d1 <= 2 (header line). Generator sweep (gmk_m3 +-t, mmk_m2/m3, gmk_hy, gmk_ub2 at small dims): no other failure. check_prog_gmk (+4 new cases) 32/64.
severity_note: Agrees (degenerate sizes, file fails to load, no corruption).
evidence: gmk_m2.c:199 `? (8 * (d[0] * d[1]) - ((d[0] < 3) ? (6 * d[1]) : 0) - ((d[1] < 3) ? (6 * d[0]) : 0))`; :212-219 remove bits {4,32,256} for d[0]<=2 and {64,128,256} for d[1]<=2: bit 256 (and more when a dimension is 1) is removed once but subtracted twice.
review_accuracy: Accurate; its 'sum per-vertex degrees' fix is what we did. The 4-neighbour formula is correct (no overlapping bit sets), as is gmk_m3's torus formula (verified: per-axis terms are disjoint).
first_pass_critique: Correct and precise about the overlap. Its closed form min(d,3) is right but replaces one formula by another; counting the mask that C_edgeOutput writes cannot drift again and lets the loop-invariant mask computation leave the loop.

extra_instances.quote: (6 * d[0] * d[1] * d[2]) - ((d[0] < 3) ? (2 * d[1] * d[2]) : 0) - ... -- correct: no diagonal arcs, per-axis removals disjoint; 27 small tori load
